pr_title: fix(rust, python): rolling_groupy was returning incorrect results when offset was positive
pr_body: There's room for optimisation, but this at least closes #9077 (besides, rolling windows looking into the future don't strike me as a common use-case)

issue_context.title: `groupby_rolling` bug for positive values of `offset`
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

Positive values of `offset` do not appear to behave as expected.  I've taken one of the the unit tests in the library, which appears to produce an incorrect result when changing `offset="1d"` to `offset="-1d"`.

I'd be keen to dig into helping fix this, but wanted to get the issue in as I'm relatively inexperienced on the rust side

### Reproducible example

```python
# Taking & minimally adapting this test: (switching offset from '-1d' to '1d)
# https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/275178c25b4bebf2f2c8a88993d445b5aabc8cc9/py-polars/tests/unit/operations/test_groupby_rolling.py#LL149C1-L163C6

import polars as pl
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "datetime": pl.date_range(
            datetime(2021, 11, 6),
            datetime(2021, 11, 9),
            "1d",
            time_zone=None,
            eager=True,
        ),
        "value": [1, 4, 9, 155],
    }
)
result = df.groupby_rolling(index_column="datetime", period="2d", offset="1d").agg(
    pl.col("value")
)
print(result)

# Output:
┌─────────────────────┬────────────────┐
│ datetime            ┆ value          │
│ ---                 ┆ ---            │
│ datetime[μs]        ┆ list[i64]      │
╞═════════════════════╪════════════════╡
│ 2021-11-06 00:00:00 ┆ [1, 4, 9, 155] │
│ 2021-11-07 00:00:00 ┆ []             │
│ 2021-11-08 00:00:00 ┆ []             │
│ 2021-11-09 00:00:00 ┆ []             │
└─────────────────────┴────────────────┘
```


### Expected behavior

I'd expect the following output:
```
┌─────────────────────┬────────────────┐
│ datetime            ┆ value          │
│ ---                 ┆ ---            │
│ datetime[μs]        ┆ list[i64]      │
╞═════════════════════╪════════════════╡
│ 2021-11-06 00:00:00 ┆ [9, 155]       │
│ 2021-11-07 00:00:00 ┆ [155]          │
│ 2021-11-08 00:00:00 ┆ []             │
│ 2021-11-09 00:00:00 ┆ []             │
└─────────────────────┴────────────────┘
```

if you have `period='2d'` and `offset='1d'`, then I think the groups should be:
- (2021-11-07, 2021-11-09]
- (2021-11-08, 2021-11-10]
- (2021-11-09, 2021-11-11]
- (2021-11-10, 2021-11-12]

which would aggregate to
- [9, 155]
- [155]

Will take a look!

review_comments:
not sure this test was right to begin with

if the dates are:
`[00:00, 00:30, ..., 3:30, 4:00]`
and the period is `2h` and the offset is `0h`, then the first window is `(00:00, 02:00]`. So that includes points: `[00:30, 01:00, 01:30, 02:00]`, i.e. the starting offset is `1`, and the length is `4`

Given that we have a nested loop now. 

Can we maybe keep the old behavior for `offset= 0`?

We can branch on the `offset=?` case and have a loop for both cases.

Or don't we hit this path on the `offset=0` case?
good call, thanks - yes, but only if the window is closed on the left (if it's open on the left, then `time[i]` shouldn't be included in the group)
